newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, palladium up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, palladium up.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Thursday, for palladium which saw a fresh four month high, but volumes were only moderate.

"It's going to be tough for gold to recover much, as producers are waiting to hedge on any bounce, but there's been a distinct lack of interest in doing very much since gold fell below $350 recently," Mitsui & Co USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.30 an ounce at $345.10, after seeing a new contract low at $344.00. Total estimated COMEX gold futures volume was 30,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted around $342.80/30, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $342.80, and the New York close Wednesday at $343.90/40.
The fundamentals remain negative for gold, analysts said.

The strength of the US dollar is pressuring demand in other currencies, potential European central bank sales are still weighing on the market, and nervous but light producer hedging has been seen from some medium sized Australian miners recently, traders said.
COMEX March silver ended down 1.5 cents at $4.857 an ounce early, though silver looked to be finding some support again around $4.800, traders said.
"Silver bounced back above $5.00 in January and clearly has some more potential than gold," Drury said.
The spot gold/silver ratio was little changed at 70.82 at Thursday's close, after falling to a nine month low at 69.79 in late January as gold slid to three year lows.
But some analysts remain bearish on silver as mine production is expected to rise later this year, when BHP's Cannington silver-lead mine in Australia comes on stream.

"This mine will produce 800 tonnes a year of silver when it reaches full production in 1998," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said. "Eight hundred tonnes in equivalent to some 55 pct of current Indian imports."

In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum closed down $1.00 at $354.50, but the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread widened to around $10.20 an ounce intraday, before ending little changed around $9.40.
NYMEX March palladium gained a further $3.00 an ounce though to $132.75.
Palladium fixed in London Thursday at $129.00 an ounce, the highest since August 1996.
Delays to Russian shipments of palladium and good refiner buying has driven up the palladium price in recent weeks, analysts said.
((-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com))
